components.note: 己 (self) — 已 looks like 己 with the gap closed, so do not mix them up. Memory aid: the opening is closed — it is already done (已经).

example.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng zǒu le.
example.english: He has already left.
example.fact: 已 is a written form of 'already' and is mostly seen in 已经 (already), 已 as 'to stop' in literary phrases like 不得已 (have no choice), and 而已 ('that's all'). Do not confuse it with 己 (jǐ, self) and 巳 (sì).

examples.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng shuì le.
examples.english: He has already gone to sleep.

examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng yǐjīng kāishǐ le.
examples.english: The movie has already started.

components.note: 夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.

example.pinyin: Tā xiàozhe duì wǒ shuōhuà.
example.english: He spoke to me with a smile.
example.fact: 笑 covers both a smile and a laugh; the difference is made with extra words, such as 微笑 (smile) and 大笑 (laugh loudly). It is also the verb for laughing at someone: 笑话 means a joke or to ridicule, so context matters.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiào qǐlái hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: She looks pretty when she smiles.

examples.hanzi: 大家都被他的话逗笑了。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu bèi tā de huà dòuxiào le.
examples.english: Everyone was made to laugh by what he said.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 进: to go and pick.
先 (xiān) is a close sound clue for xuǎn; 先 also in 洗 xǐ.

example.pinyin: Nǐ xuǎn nǎ yí gè?
example.english: Which one do you choose?
example.fact: 选 is a verb for picking among options and forms 选择 (to choose; a choice), 选手 (contestant) and 选举 (election). It is often used with a resultative: 选好了 ('have chosen'), 选中 ('have picked out').

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xuǎn zhège lán sè de.
examples.english: I'll pick this blue one.

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā xuǎn tā dāng bānzhǎng.
examples.english: Everyone elected him class monitor.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,我感到很惊讶。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, wǒ gǎndào hěn jīngyà.
example.english: Hearing this news, I felt very surprised.
example.fact: 感到 almost always introduces an emotional or sensory state via a following adjective or clause (感到惊讶, 感到高兴) and reads noticeably more formal than the everyday 觉得 — in casual speech 觉得 dominates, while 感到 shows up more in narration, news reports, and writing.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎndào yǒudiǎn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: I feel a bit nervous.

examples.pinyin: Tā gǎndào hěn gūdān.
examples.english: He feels very lonely.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 部 part. 那 was a place name before it meant "that".
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yǐzi fàng dào nàbian.
example.english: Please put the chair over there.
example.fact: 那边 pairs with 这边 ("over here") as Mandarin’s directional near/far duo built on location rather than a demonstrative pronoun — where 那里/这里 point at a place as a noun ("that place"), 那边/这边 point at a side or direction, often used together with a pointing gesture.

examples.pinyin: Nàbian de rén shì shéi?
examples.english: Who is that person over there?

examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào zài mǎlù nàbian.
examples.english: The school is on the other side of the road.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and distance, as in 过, 近, 进: 远 is a road that goes far.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuǎn; 元 also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn yuǎn.
example.english: My home is far from school.
example.fact: To say 'far from', Chinese uses 离 before the place and 远 after: 离这儿很远. Its opposite is 近 (jìn, near). It can also mean 'by far' in comparison patterns: 远比…好 ('far better than').

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ lí huǒchēzhàn bù yuǎn.
examples.english: It's not far from here to the train station.

examples.hanzi: 他住得很远，每天坐地铁上班。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhù de hěn yuǎn, měitiān zuò dìtiě shàngbān.
examples.english: He lives far away and takes the subway to work every day.

components.note: 儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.pinyin: Tā yǒu yí gè érzi.
example.english: He has a son.
example.fact: 儿 is most often seen as the suffix in northern speech, such as 花儿 and 玩儿, where it gives a rhotic 'r' sound to the syllable. As a word on its own, it means child or son, as in 儿子 and 儿童 (children).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí ge xiǎo nǚ'ér.
examples.english: I have a little daughter.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài zhèr děng wǒ yíhuìr.
examples.english: Wait for me here for a moment.

components.note: 古 (gǔ) is a close sound clue for gù; 古 also in 姑 gū and 固 gù.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: an action with a cause.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 妈妈每天晚上给我讲一个故事。
example.pinyin: Māma měitiān wǎnshang gěi wǒ jiǎng yí gè gùshi.
example.english: Mom tells me a story every night.
example.fact: The everyday sense "story, tale" is read with a neutral tone on 事 (gùshi). Dictionaries also list the same two characters read with a full fourth tone, gùshì, for a separate, much rarer classical/literary sense, "a precedent, an old practice" — it is the common neutral-tone reading, not the toned classical one, that accounts for this word’s high frequency here.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge yǒuqù de gùshi.
examples.english: This is an interesting story.

examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan gěi háizi jiǎng gùshi.
examples.english: He likes telling stories to children.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — illness, as in 病 sick, 痛 pain, 疼 ache: madness is an illness.
风 (fēng, wind) gives the exact sound; also in 枫 fēng.

example.pinyin: Tā hǎoxiàng fēng le.
example.english: He seems to have gone crazy.
example.fact: 疯 can be literal (疯子, a madman) but is also very colloquial for intense enthusiasm: 疯狂 (crazy, frenzied), 玩疯了 ('played like crazy') and 疯了 (as in 'I'm going nuts!').

examples.hanzi: 你疯了吗？这么冷还游泳！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ fēng le ma? Zhème lěng hái yóuyǒng!
examples.english: Are you crazy? Swimming in this cold!

examples.pinyin: Háizimen fēng wánle yì zhěng tiān.
examples.english: The kids played wildly all day.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 换 is to swap with the hands.
奂 (huàn) — same sound — 换 is huàn, like 奂; 奂 also sounds out 唤 huàn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng huàn yíxià zuòwèi.
example.english: I'd like to change seats.
example.fact: 换 means to replace one thing with another, not to alter it: 换衣服 (change clothes), 换钱 (exchange money), 换车 (change trains). For 'to change' in the sense of becoming different, Chinese uses 变 instead.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng huàn yí jiàn dà yìdiǎn de.
examples.english: I'd like to swap for a slightly bigger one.

examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, zài nǎlǐ kěyǐ huàn qián?
examples.english: Excuse me, where can I exchange money?

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
昏 (hūn, dusk) gives the exact sound; weddings were traditionally held at dusk, so the sound clue is also a meaning clue.

example.pinyin: Tāmen dǎsuàn míngnián jiéhūn.
example.english: They plan to get married next year.
example.fact: 结婚 is a verb-object compound (结 "to tie" + 婚 "marriage") that cannot take a person directly as its object — "to marry someone" has to be phrased with 跟/和 + person + 结婚 (我跟她结婚, never 我结婚她), a common structural trap for English speakers used to "marry" taking a direct object.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen qùnián jiéhūn le.
examples.english: They got married last year.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiéhūn le ma?
examples.english: Are you married?

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 犭 is the animal radical (犬), as in 猫, 狗, 狼; 猜 once meant a suspicious, wary animal.
青 (qīng) — near sound — 猜 is cāi; 青 also sounds out 清, 请, 情 and 晴.

example.pinyin: Nǐ cāi wǒ zài xiǎng shénme?
example.english: Guess what I'm thinking.
example.fact: 猜 is the usual verb for guessing: 猜谜 (guess a riddle), 猜对了 (guessed right) and 猜测 (to speculate). In the game 猜拳 (rock-paper-scissors) it means to play a guessing hand game.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ cāi tā jīnnián duō dà?
examples.english: Guess how old he is this year.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ cāi tā búhuì lái le.
examples.english: I guess he won't come anymore.

meanings: (dialect) (in a coaxing or familiar way) you

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: a spoken pronoun.
自 (zì) is only a loose sound clue for zán.
亻 (person) — marks words about people, as in 你 you, 他 he, 做 do. Here it shows 们 pluralises person words (我们, 他们).
门 (mén) gives the sound: 们 is men (neutral tone), the same syllable as 门 gate.

example.pinyin: Zánmen yìqǐ qù chīfàn ba.
example.english: Let’s go eat together (you and I both).
example.fact: 咱们 is a northern-Mandarin variant of 我们 that many speakers still keep a distinction for: 咱们 is strictly inclusive, guaranteed to include the listener ("we, you and I"), while 我们 is ambiguous and can exclude the person being spoken to — a distinction English "we" doesn’t make at all.

examples.pinyin: Zánmen míngtiān qù páshān, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Shall we go hiking tomorrow?

examples.pinyin: Bié kèqi, zánmen shì yì jiā rén.
examples.english: Don't be polite, we're family.

components.note: 木 (wood) — beds were wooden frames; 木 is the radical of trees and wooden things like 桌 table and 椅 chair.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tǎng zài chuáng shang.
example.english: I want to lie on the bed.
example.fact: 床 uses the measure word 张 (一张床) and doubles up as a measure for bedding, like 一床被子 (a quilt). It forms compounds like 起床 (get up), 床单 (bed sheet) and 病床 (hospital bed).

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng chuáng yòu dà yòu shūfu.
examples.english: This bed is big and comfortable.

examples.pinyin: Háizi qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
examples.english: The child gets up at seven.

meanings: to treat sth by a special process

components.note: 夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ huì jǐnkuài chǔlǐ.
example.english: I will handle this matter as soon as possible.
example.fact: 处理 is the neutral, businesslike verb for handling a problem, task, or file — used everywhere from customer service (处理投诉, "handle complaints") to computing (数据处理, "data processing") — sitting a register above the casual 办 ("to do, handle") and below the heavier 解决 (also in this batch), which implies actually resolving something rather than just attending to it.

examples.hanzi: 我不知道怎么处理这件事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào zěnme chǔlǐ zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: I don't know how to handle this.

examples.pinyin: Tā chǔlǐ wèntí hěn lěngjìng.
examples.english: He handles problems very calmly.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐; oldest form shows a hand arranging a woman's hair, a wife.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Tā de qīzi shì yì míng yīshēng.
example.english: His wife is a doctor.
example.fact: With a neutral tone on 子, qīzi is the everyday word for "wife." The same two characters read with a full third tone, qīzǐ, name a separate, more literary sense, "wife and children" — the ordinary neutral-tone reading, not the toned literary one, is what makes 妻子 this common.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qīzi zhèngzài zuòfàn.
examples.english: My wife is cooking.

examples.pinyin: Tā hěn ài tā de qīzi.
examples.english: He loves his wife very much.

meanings: (of an army etc) to be on the march

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.pinyin: Huìyì zhèngzài jìnxíng.
example.english: The meeting is currently underway.
example.fact: 进行 is a formal, often bureaucratic-sounding verb that turns almost any action noun into a full verb phrase (进行调查 "carry out an investigation," 进行讨论 "hold a discussion") — a productive pattern common in news and official writing that lets a two-character noun stand in for a verb English would express more simply, like "investigate" or "discuss."

examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò jìnxíng de hěn shùnlì.
examples.english: The work is going smoothly.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiāng jìnxíng yí cì diàochá.
examples.english: We will carry out a survey.

components.note: 内 (inside) — a person or something entering 入 inside an enclosure 冂: inside, as in 内容.

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài nèibù shǐyòng.
example.english: Please use this internally.
example.fact: 内 is a formal word for 'inside' and 'within', as in 国内 (domestic), 内容 (content), 内心 (inner heart) and 一周内 (within a week). Its opposite is 外 (wài, outside).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài sān tiān nèi huífù wǒ.
examples.english: Please reply to me within three days.

examples.hanzi: 这个房间内有一张桌子。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān nèi yǒu yì zhāng zhuōzi.
examples.english: There is a table inside this room.

components.note: 日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.
不 (bù) is a loose sound clue for fǒu and gives the meaning "not".
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: saying no.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào tā shìfǒu huì lái.
example.english: I don’t know whether he will come.
example.fact: 是否 is the formal, written-register equivalent of the everyday spoken 是不是 or the simpler "V不V" pattern — reach for 是否 in a report or essay, and for 是不是 in conversation; using 是否 in casual chat can sound stiff, and 是不是 in a formal document can sound too colloquial.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shìfǒu tóngyì wǒ de kànfǎ?
examples.english: Do you agree with my view?

examples.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ shìfǒu yǒu kòng.
examples.english: Please tell me whether you're free.

components.note: 殳 (strike) — 殳 is a hand with a tool striking, as in 毁, 殴; 段 is a piece cut off a larger whole, and sounds out 锻 duàn.

example.pinyin: Zhè duàn lù hěn nán zǒu.
example.english: This stretch of road is hard to walk.
example.fact: 段 is both a noun and a measure word for portions: 一段时间 (a period of time), 一段话 (a passage of speech) and 段落 (paragraph). It is also a surname.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dúle zhè duàn wénzhāng liǎng biàn.
examples.english: I read this paragraph twice.

examples.pinyin: Dào chēzhàn hái yǒu yí duàn lù.
examples.english: There's still some distance to the station.

components.note: 令 (order) — a person kneeling under a command from above. Its sound spreads to 冷 lěng, 零 líng, 铃 líng, 领 lǐng and 怜 lián.

example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi lìng rén gāoxìng.
example.english: This news makes people happy.
example.fact: 令 is a literary causative verb, most often seen in the pattern 令人 + adjective ('to make one feel…'), such as 令人高兴 and 令人失望. It also means 'an order' in 命令 and 口令 (password, command), and is an honorific prefix in 令尊.

examples.hanzi: 他的成绩令老师很满意。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì lìng lǎoshī hěn mǎnyì.
examples.english: His grades made the teacher very satisfied.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息令大家很吃惊。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi lìng dàjiā hěn chījīng.
examples.english: This news surprised everyone.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: hard enough to cut.
冈 (gāng) gives the exact sound; also in 钢 gāng and 纲 gāng.
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: hard enough to cut.
冈 (gāng) gives the exact sound; also in 钢 gāng and 纲 gāng.

example.pinyin: Tā gānggang líkāi.
example.english: He just left.
example.fact: 刚刚 is 刚 ("just, a moment ago") reduplicated for emphasis, the same doubling device behind 谢谢 (seen in the pilot batch) — the doubled form sharpens the sense of recency compared to the plain, slightly less emphatic 刚 alone.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gānggāng chīguo fàn.
examples.english: I've just eaten.

examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng gānggāng kāishǐ.
examples.english: The movie has just started.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 警察还在调查这个案子。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá hái zài diàochá zhège ànzi.
example.english: The police are still investigating this case.
example.fact: 案 by itself already meant a low wooden table or desk in antiquity, the kind an official might set documents on while reviewing a dispute — a traditional explanation for how 案子/案件 came to mean "a (legal) case" in modern usage, an object-turned-abstraction not unlike English "the case is on my desk."

examples.pinyin: Zhège ànzi hěn fùzá.
examples.english: This case is very complicated.

examples.pinyin: Fǎguān zhèngzài kàn zhège ànzi.
examples.english: The judge is reviewing this case.

components.note: 彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 我们必须马上采取行动。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen bìxū mǎshàng cǎiqǔ xíngdòng.
example.english: We must take action immediately.
example.fact: 行动 most often appears as the object of the fixed verb 采取 ("采取行动," "to take action") rather than standing alone as a verb in everyday speech — one of many two-character nouns in Mandarin that habitually pair with one specific "light verb" rather than combining freely with any verb of doing.

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā de xíngdòng dōu hěn kuài.
examples.english: Everyone acted quickly.

examples.hanzi: 他的腿受伤了,行动不方便。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ shòushāng le, xíngdòng bù fāngbiàn.
examples.english: His leg is hurt, so moving around is inconvenient.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips, once used for writing and lists, as in 等 wait, 笔 pen, 笑 laugh.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; 弟 also sounds out 梯 tī and 剃 tì.
二 (two) — two parallel strokes: the next step after 一 and before 三.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ dì èr cì lái Běijīng.
example.english: This is the second time I’ve come to Beijing.
example.fact: 第 is a dedicated ordinal-number prefix with no meaning of its own outside this role — attach it to any cardinal number (第一, 第二, 第三...) to turn "one, two, three" into "first, second, third," a far more regular system than English’s mix of "-th" endings and irregular forms like "first" and "second."

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì dì èr ge wèntí.
examples.english: This is the second question.

examples.hanzi: 第二天早上,他很早就起床了。
examples.pinyin: Dì èr tiān zǎoshang, tā hěn zǎo jiù qǐchuáng le.
examples.english: The next morning, he got up very early.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 动: to exert strength.
奴 (nú) is a close sound clue for nǔ; 奴 also in 怒 nù.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 你只要努力,就一定能成功。
example.pinyin: Nǐ zhǐyào nǔlì, jiù yídìng néng chénggōng.
example.english: As long as you try hard, you’ll definitely succeed.
example.fact: 努力 functions equally well as a verb ("to work hard"), an adverb modifying another verb (努力学习, "study hard"), and an adjective describing a person (他很努力, "he’s hard-working") — one Mandarin word doing the job of three different English parts of speech.

examples.pinyin: Tā xuéxí hěn nǔlì.
examples.english: He studies very hard.

examples.hanzi: 我会努力完成这个工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì nǔlì wánchéng zhège gōngzuò.
examples.english: I'll try hard to finish this job.

components.note: 害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: fear is a feeling.
白 (bái) is a close sound clue for pà; 白 also in 拍 pāi and 伯 bó.

example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi hěn hàipà dǎléi.
example.english: Small children are very afraid of thunder.
example.fact: 害怕 takes its feared object directly, as if it were an ordinary transitive verb (害怕打雷, "afraid of thunder"; 害怕黑暗, "afraid of the dark") — where English inserts "of" between the adjective "afraid" and its object, Chinese just runs the two together with no preposition needed.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú hàipà hēi'àn.
examples.english: I'm not afraid of the dark.

examples.pinyin: Tā hàipà yí ge rén zuò fēijī.
examples.english: She's afraid of flying alone.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks and flavors: 醉 drunk, 醒 sober, 酸 sour, 配 match; 酒 is liquor, with 氵 for the liquid.
酉 also hints at the sound: yǒu is close to jiǔ.

example.pinyin: Tā bù hē jiǔ.
example.english: He doesn't drink alcohol.
example.fact: 酒 is the general word for any alcoholic drink, not only wine: 白酒 (baijiu), 啤酒 (beer), 红酒 (red wine). In compounds like 酒店 it means 'hotel' in Chinese, though 'wine shop' is its original sense.

examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang wǒ bù xiǎng hē jiǔ.
examples.english: I don't want to drink alcohol tonight.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu yì píng hóngjiǔ.
examples.english: There's a bottle of red wine on the table.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).

example.pinyin: Tā gěi wǒ fāle yì tiáo xiāoxi.
example.english: He sent me a message.
example.fact: 发 has a huge range: 发短信 (send a text), 发烧 (have a fever), 发财 (get rich), 发现 (discover) and 出发 (set off). As a separate character 发 (fà) means hair, as in 头发, which is the same simplified character with a different reading.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ fā yóujiàn ba.
examples.english: I'll send you an email.

examples.pinyin: Gōngsī fāle xīn de gōngzuòfú.
examples.english: The company issued new work uniforms.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢.
周 (zhōu) is a loose sound clue for diào/tiáo; 周 also in 凋 diāo.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 查 first meant a raft of wood. 查 also gives 渣 zhā and 楂 zhā.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查这起事故的原因。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ shìgù de yuányīn.
example.english: The police are investigating the cause of this accident.
example.fact: 调查 covers everything from a formal police or journalistic investigation to a casual opinion poll (民意调查, "public opinion survey") — English splits this range across several words ("investigation," "inquiry," "survey," "poll"), while Chinese keeps one verb for the whole family of "systematically finding things out."

examples.hanzi: 我们做了一次市场调查。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuòle yí cì shìchǎng diàochá.
examples.english: We did a market survey.

examples.hanzi: 警察开始调查他的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá kāishǐ diàochá tā de péngyou.
examples.english: The police began investigating his friend.

components.note: 夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.
土 (earth) — the top part, the ground family as in 地, 场, 块. Memory aid: leave the ground 土 and go off on your own 厶 path.
厶 (private, small loop) — the bottom part. Old forms show a person leaving a place, so the 土 story is only a mnemonic.

example.hanzi: 他失去了一个很好的机会。
example.pinyin: Tā shīqù le yí gè hěn hǎo de jīhuì.
example.english: He lost a really good opportunity.
example.fact: 失去 is reserved for losing something abstract or irreplaceable — a chance, someone’s trust, a limb, a loved one — while the everyday verb for misplacing a physical object, like keys or an umbrella, is 丢 (丢钥匙, "lose one’s keys") — a distinction with no single equivalent in English "to lose."

examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng shīqù zhè fèn gōngzuò.
examples.english: He doesn't want to lose this job.

examples.pinyin: Tā shīqùle zìjǐ de shǒujī.
examples.english: She lost her phone.

components.note: 欠 (yawn, open mouth) — 欠 shows a person with an open mouth, as in 吹 blow, 欢 joyful; 歌 is the mouth opened in song.
哥 (gē) — same sound — 歌 is gē, just like 哥; 哥 means elder brother.

example.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē hěn hǎotīng.
example.english: This song sounds great.
example.fact: 歌 takes the measure word 首 (一首歌), and the verb is 唱: 唱歌 (to sing). It forms 歌手 (singer), 歌曲 (song) and 儿歌 (children's song).

examples.pinyin: Tā chàngle yì shǒu Zhōngwén gē.
examples.english: She sang a Chinese song.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan tīng shénme gē?
examples.english: What songs do you like to listen to?

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: achievement takes effort.
工 (gōng) gives the exact sound; 工 also means work.

example.hanzi: 经过多次尝试,他终于成功了。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò duō cì chángshì, tā zhōngyú chénggōng le.
example.english: After many attempts, he finally succeeded.
example.fact: 成功 doubles as a stative verb ("to succeed," 成功了) and an adjective meaning "successful" (一个成功的人, "a successful person") without changing form — one more example, alongside 工作 in the pilot batch, of a Chinese word crossing freely between verb and adjective roles that English keeps grammatically separate ("succeed" vs. "successful").

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ chénggōng!
examples.english: Wishing you success!

examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shìyàn hěn chénggōng.
examples.english: This experiment was very successful.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — mouth radical for speaking and sounds, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 唱 is to sing.
昌 (chāng) — same sound, different tone — 唱 is chàng; 昌 also sounds out 倡 chàng.

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan chànggē.
example.english: She likes to sing.
example.fact: 唱 is the verb for singing and for performing opera, as in 唱京剧. It also means to call out, as in 唱名 and, in slang, 唱反调 (to take the opposite stance).

examples.pinyin: Tā zài yùshì lǐ chànggē.
examples.english: He is singing in the bathroom.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng gěi wǒmen chàng yì shǒu ma?
examples.english: Can you sing one for us?

components.note: 耂 (old) — shown in 老 old and 者; 考 first meant an aged person (the same word as 老), then to examine.
丂 (kǎo) gives the sound; also in 巧 qiǎo, 烤 kǎo and 拷 kǎo.
心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 虑 is to turn something over in the mind.

example.hanzi: 我需要考虑一下再决定。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào kǎolǜ yíxià zài juédìng.
example.english: I need to think it over before deciding.
example.fact: 考虑 is built from 考 ("to examine, test") and 虑 ("to worry, deliberate") — two characters that separately name "scrutinizing" and "turning something over anxiously in the mind," compounding into the even-handed modern sense "to consider, think over."

examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒ kǎolǜ yíxià hǎo ma?
examples.english: Can you let me think about it?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu kǎolǜguo bānjiā?
examples.english: Have you ever considered moving?

meanings: just now (variant of 剛才|刚才[gang1 cai2])

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: hard enough to cut.
冈 (gāng) gives the exact sound; also in 钢 gāng and 纲 gāng.
才 (talent, just) — a sprout pushing out of the ground. 才 also sounds out 材 cái and 财 cái.

example.pinyin: Gāngcái shì shéi zài qiāo mén?
example.english: Who was knocking on the door just now?
example.fact: 刚才 and its near-twin 刚刚 (also in this batch) both mean "just now," but 刚才 usually points to a slightly looser stretch of recent time — anywhere from moments to an hour ago — and can stand alone as an answer to "when," while 刚刚 emphasizes the very instant something happened and almost always attaches directly to the verb it modifies.

examples.pinyin: Tā gāngcái hái zài zhèr ne.
examples.english: He was still here just now.

examples.hanzi: 我刚才说的话你听清楚了吗?
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gāngcái shuō de huà nǐ tīng qīngchu le ma?
examples.english: Did you hear clearly what I just said?

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and binding, as in 红, 给, 经: an agreement binds like a cord.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for yuē; 勺 also in 药 yào and 钓 diào.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.pinyin: Wǒmen jīnwǎn yǒu yí gè yuēhuì.
example.english: We have a date tonight.
example.fact: 约会 covers both a romantic "date" and a plain scheduled "appointment," a broader range than English keeps in one word — context alone, such as talking about a doctor’s office versus talking about a crush, tells a listener which sense is meant.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng hé tā yuēhuì.
examples.english: I'd like to go on a date with her.

examples.hanzi: 明天下午我有一个约会。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān xiàwǔ wǒ yǒu yí ge yuēhuì.
examples.english: I have an appointment tomorrow afternoon.

components.note: 艹 stands in for 竹 (bamboo) in the traditional 節, bamboo joints: sections, then festivals and knots.
目 (eye) — an eye turned on its side. As a radical it marks sight: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睡 sleep, 盯 stare.

example.hanzi: 你最喜欢哪个电视节目?
example.pinyin: Nǐ zuì xǐhuan nǎge diànshì jiémù?
example.english: Which TV show do you like best?
example.fact: 目 by itself is a pictograph of an eye — in 节目, that "eye" sits beside 节 (originally a bamboo joint, later "a division, a section"), giving the compound its literal sense of a discrete segment set before an audience’s eyes, and its modern meaning "program, show."

examples.pinyin: Zhège jiémù hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: This show is very interesting.

examples.hanzi: 春节晚会有很多好看的节目。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié wǎnhuì yǒu hěn duō hǎokàn de jiémù.
examples.english: The Spring Festival gala has many great acts.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.pinyin: Tā tōngguò le zhè cì kǎoshì.
example.english: He passed this exam.
example.fact: 通过 slides between three related jobs in one word: a verb meaning "to pass" (通过考试, "pass an exam"), a verb meaning "to approve, adopt" (通过决议, "pass a resolution"), and a preposition meaning "by means of, via" (通过努力, "through hard work") — context, not form, tells a listener which one is in play.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen tōngguò diànhuà liánxì.
examples.english: We keep in touch by phone.

examples.hanzi: 他通过努力得到了机会。
examples.pinyin: Tā tōngguò nǔlì dédàole jīhuì.
examples.english: He earned the opportunity through effort.

components.note: 之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".
门 (gate) — doors and openings, as in 问 ask, 开 open, 关 close.
日 (sun) — a gap in the gate lets daylight through (the traditional 間 had 月 moon): the space between.

example.hanzi: 中国和日本之间隔着一片大海。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó hé Rìběn zhījiān gézhe yí piàn dà hǎi.
example.english: A great expanse of sea lies between China and Japan.
example.fact: 之 is a literary, almost fossilized possessive particle — its everyday equivalent is the far more common 的 — but 之间 (like 之前 "before" and 之后 "after") keeps this old-fashioned 之 alive as a fixed set phrase rather than as a rule a learner can extend freely.

examples.hanzi: 我家在学校和公司之间。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài xuéxiào hé gōngsī zhījiān.
examples.english: My home is between the school and the company.

examples.hanzi: 朋友之间应该互相帮助。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou zhījiān yīnggāi hùxiāng bāngzhù.
examples.english: Friends should help each other.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".
白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.

example.pinyin: Nǐ hái xūyào biéde dōngxi ma?
example.english: Do you need anything else?
example.fact: 别的 is the everyday, spoken-register word for "other, else" (别的东西, 别的人), while its near-synonym 其他 reads a shade more formal and shows up more often in writing and set expressions (其他人, 其他情况) — close enough in meaning that a learner can usually swap one for the other without changing what a sentence means, just its register.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ hái xiǎng chī biéde ma?
examples.english: Do you want to eat anything else?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu biéde bànfǎ.
examples.english: I have no other way.

components.note: 子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zài xué Zhōngwén.
example.english: I am learning Chinese.
example.fact: 学 is a verb ('to learn') and also a suffix for fields: 数学 (math), 科学 (science), 大学 (university), 学生 (student). 学 and 习 combine as 学习 (to study), the usual way to say 'study'.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué xué yī.
examples.english: She studies medicine at university.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xué zuò Zhōngguó cài.
examples.english: I want to learn how to cook Chinese food.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān wánr de hěn kāixīn.
example.english: Today was a lot of fun.
example.fact: 开心 pictures happiness almost literally — 开 ("to open") plus 心 ("heart"), "an opened-up heart" — a transparent compositional image sitting right alongside its near-synonym 高兴, the more neutral, general-purpose word for "happy" in everyday Mandarin.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒmen guò de hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: We had a great time today.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào bù kāixīn, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Don't be unhappy, okay?

components.note: 母 (mother) — a woman 女 with two dots for breasts: a nursing mother. 母 also appears in 每 měi, 海 hǎi and 梅 méi.
亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.

example.pinyin: Mǔqīn jié kuàilè!
example.english: Happy Mother’s Day!
example.fact: 母亲 is the formal, written-register word for "mother," reserved for essays, official contexts, and set phrases like 母亲节 ("Mother’s Day") — in daily conversation Chinese speakers overwhelmingly say 妈妈 instead, much like English speakers default to "mom" over the more formal "mother" in casual speech.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǔqīn zài yīyuàn gōngzuò.
examples.english: My mother works at a hospital.

examples.pinyin: Mǔqīn měitiān gěi wǒmen zuòfàn.
examples.english: Mother cooks for us every day.

components.note: 车 (cart, vehicle) — marks wheeled things, as in 转, 轮, 较; 辆 counts vehicles.
两 (liǎng) hints at the sound: 辆 liàng is close.

example.pinyin: Ménkǒu yǒu yí liàng chē.
example.english: There is a car at the door.
example.fact: 辆 is the measure word for vehicles with wheels: 一辆车, 一辆自行车 (bicycle), 一辆公共汽车 (bus). For airplanes and boats, Chinese uses different words (架, 艘).

examples.pinyin: Lùshang yǒu hěn duō liàng qìchē.
examples.english: There are many cars on the road.

examples.pinyin: Tā mǎile yí liàng xīn zìxíngchē.
examples.english: He bought a new bicycle.

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 我们再想想别的主意吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài xiǎngxiang biéde zhǔyi ba.
example.english: Let’s think of some other ideas.
example.fact: 主意 names a practical plan or decision one settles on (拿主意, "make up one’s mind"; 出主意, "suggest an idea/plan") rather than an abstract thought or concept, which is instead 想法 or 观念 — 主意 is the "idea" you act on, not the "idea" you merely have.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì ge hǎo zhǔyi!
examples.english: That's a good idea!

examples.pinyin: Nǐ nádìng zhǔyi le ma?
examples.english: Have you made up your mind?

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 探 is to reach out and feel, then to explore.
The right half is a sound part shared with 深 shēn: a loose clue for tàn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ qù tànwàng péngyou.
example.english: I am going to visit a friend.
example.fact: 探 describes reaching out to find something: 探索 (explore), 探险 (adventure), 探望 (visit someone ill) and 探头 (stick one's head out). In daily speech it is more often seen inside compounds than on its own.

examples.pinyin: Tā qù yīyuàn tànwàng nǎinai.
examples.english: She went to the hospital to visit grandma.

examples.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan tànxiǎn.
examples.english: Kids love exploring adventures.

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand stretched with a measuring rule: 丈 is a unit of length (ten 尺), and in 丈夫 the old word for "husband".
大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.

example.pinyin: Tā de zhàngfu zài guówài gōngzuò.
example.english: Her husband works abroad.
example.fact: 丈 doubles as a unit of length (about 3.3 meters) and, in older usage, a mark of seniority or full adulthood — the same 丈 shows up in 丈人 ("father-in-law") and 老丈 ("old man"). 丈夫, traditionally glossed as "a person of full-grown stature," narrowed over time from a general term for a grown man to today’s specific meaning, "husband."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhàngfu xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
examples.english: My husband likes playing soccer.

examples.hanzi: 她的丈夫很会照顾孩子。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhàngfu hěn huì zhàogù háizi.
examples.english: Her husband is good at looking after the kids.

components.note: 又 (hand) — the bottom, standing in for the 攴 (tap) of traditional 變. 亦 on top replaces the tangled-thread part and has no meaning link.
變 (traditional) — tangled threads and a tapping hand 攴: sorting out a mess, so 'change'. Read as 'usually explained'.
成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.

example.hanzi: 毛毛虫最后变成了蝴蝶。
example.pinyin: Máomaochóng zuìhòu biànchéng le húdié.
example.english: The caterpillar eventually turned into a butterfly.
example.fact: 成 works here as a resultative complement meaning "into a completed new state" — 变成 literally "change into," in contrast to the bare verb 变 ("to change"), which only says something is changing without specifying what it changes into.

examples.pinyin: Tiānqì biànchéngle yīntiān.
examples.english: The weather turned cloudy.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng bǎ àihào biànchéng gōngzuò.
examples.english: He wants to turn his hobby into a job.

components.note: 彳 (step, left foot) — walking and roads: 行, 往, 很, 得; 待 is to go toward and wait on someone.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue; its family varies: 诗 shī, 持 chí, 特 tè, 等 děng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zài jiā dāi yì tiān.
example.english: I want to stay home for a day.
example.fact: 待 has two main readings: dāi ('to stay', colloquial, as in 待在家) and dài ('to treat, to wait', as in 对待, 等待, 招待). The 'stay' sense is often written 呆 in casual writing, so both forms appear online.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zài Běijīng dāi yí ge yuè.
examples.english: I want to stay in Beijing for a month.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié dāi zài nàlǐ, kuài guòlái.
examples.english: Don't stay there, come over quickly.
